legend: Thanos sort is one of the sorting algorithms that works in time linear in the length of the array.
The sorting algorithm is as follows:

1) If the array a=(a1,⋯,an)$$$a = (a_1, \cdots , a_n)$$$ is already sorted, then the process stops. An array is considered sorted if for every i$$$i$$$ from 2$$$2$$$ to n$$$n$$$, it holds that ai−1≤ai$$$a_{i-1} \le a_i$$$.

2) Otherwise, either the first ⌈n2⌉$$$\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$$$ elements of the array or the last ⌊n2⌋$$$\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor$$$ elements are chosen uniformly at random. All of them are removed, and the algorithm proceeds to step 1.

Since many elements may disappear during Thanos sort, for an array a$$$a$$$, let f(a)$$$f(a)$$$ be the expected number of elements remaining in the final array.

input: The first line contains two integers n,q$$$n, q$$$ (1≤n,q≤106$$$1 \le n, q \le 10^6$$$) – the length of the array and the number of queries, respectively.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an(0≤ai≤109)$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\, (0 \le a_i \le 10^9)$$$ – the initial values of the array a$$$a$$$.
